items.markdown:
If you’re looking for a **blue Staffordshire Bull Terrier (“Staffy”) puppy in the UK**, I’d start with breeders listed through [thekennelclub.org.uk](https://www.thekennelclub.org.uk/search/find-an-assured-breeder/?utm_source=chatgpt.com) rather than relying on general puppy-sale adverts. Blue is an accepted Staffordshire Bull Terrier colour under the current breed standard. [The Kennel Club](https://www.thekennelclub.org.uk/search/breeds-a-to-z/breeds/terrier/staffordshire-bull-terrier/?gad=1&utm_source=chatgpt.com) 

A few local listings showed up around the wider High Wycombe/Bucks area, including Turners Wood Kennels in Chalfont St Giles and [Trojanbulls Staffordshire bull terrier licenced breeder and Champion stud dogs](https://www.trojanstaffuk.com/) in Basingstoke. **I wouldn't treat a business listing or its reviews as evidence that a particular breeder is responsible**, though—I'd independently verify their health testing, licensing and breeding practices.

## What to ask the breeder

For a Staffy, I'd specifically ask:

- **“Can I see the mother's health-test certificates and the father's?”** The Kennel Club recommends DNA testing for **hereditary cataracts (HC-HSF4-2)** and **L-2-HGA**, plus elbow and eye screening for the breed. [The Kennel Club](https://www.thekennelclub.org.uk/search/breeds-a-to-z/breeds/terrier/staffordshire-bull-terrier/?gad=1&utm_source=chatgpt.com) [The Kennel Club](https://www.thekennelclub.org.uk/media/qvffqvwg/kc_health_standard.pdf?utm_source=chatgpt.com)
- **“Can I verify those results on the Kennel Club's Health Test Results Finder?”** Don't settle for “both parents are health tested” without seeing the actual results. [The Kennel Club](https://www.thekennelclub.org.uk/dog-breeding/first-time-breeders/health-screening-a-step-by-step-guide/?utm_source=chatgpt.com)
- **“Can I meet the puppy with its mother at the place it was raised?”** You should see the dam and the puppy yourself before paying a deposit. The Kennel Club specifically recommends this. [The Kennel Club](https://www.thekennelclub.org.uk/search/find-an-assured-breeder/?utm_source=chatgpt.com)
- **“How old is the mother, and how many litters has she had?”**
- **“Have there been skin problems, L-2-HGA, cataracts, elbow problems or other significant health problems in the parents, siblings or previous litters?”** Skin conditions and L-2-HGA are identified as key breed health priorities. [The Kennel Club](https://www.thekennelclub.org.uk/search/breeds-a-to-z/breeds/terrier/staffordshire-bull-terrier/?gad=1&utm_source=chatgpt.com)
- **“What socialisation have the puppies had?”** Ask about household noises, visitors, children, other dogs, handling, car travel and being left briefly alone.
- **“What vaccinations, worming and vet checks have been done, and can I have the records?”** [The Kennel Club](https://www.thekennelclub.org.uk/dog-breeding/first-time-breeders/selling-your-puppies/?utm_source=chatgpt.com)
- **“What food are they eating and what routine are they used to?”**
- **“What happens if I can no longer keep the dog?”** A good breeder should care about the dog's lifetime welfare rather than simply completing the sale.
- **“Are the puppies Kennel Club registered, and can I see the registration details for the parents?”**

### One important point about “blue”

I'd be wary of anyone marketing a puppy primarily as **“rare blue,” “exclusive blue,” or “blue Staffies”** and charging a large premium purely for the colour. Blue itself is an accepted colour, so the important questions are the puppy's **health, temperament, breeding and socialisation**, not how unusual the coat is. [The Kennel Club](https://www.thekennelclub.org.uk/search/breeds-a-to-z/breeds/terrier/staffordshire-bull-terrier/?gad=1&utm_source=chatgpt.com) 

Also avoid breeders producing **merle Staffies**: The Kennel Club says merle puppies from relevant matings aren't registered because of associated vision and hearing risks. [The Kennel Club](https://www.thekennelclub.org.uk/search/breeds-a-to-z/breeds/terrier/staffordshire-bull-terrier/?gad=1&utm_source=chatgpt.com) 

If you tell me roughly **how far you're willing to travel from High Wycombe (e.g. 30, 60 or 100 miles)**, I can look for currently advertised blue Staffy litters and help you separate the promising breeders from the red flags.
